User.title: User

email.description: Unique email address of the administrator.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the user account was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the project record was last updated.

definition.description: Collection for storing administrator user profiles. Used for DBAC (Database-Backed Access Control) to verify admin role based on `request.auth.uid` for all CMS operations. Includes denormalized 'role' field for authorization independence.

params.name: adminId
params.description: The unique ID of the administrator, corresponding to `request.auth.uid`.

definition.description: Collection for Rohan Bodkhe's portfolio projects. Documents are publicly readable (if status is 'completed' or 'ongoing' as enforced by rules) and only writable by the administrator. Includes 'status' and 'featured' fields for public filtering.

Collection for blog posts. Documents are publicly readable (if status is 'published' as enforced by rules) and only writable by the administrator. Utilizes a 'status' field for explicit state modeling (draft/published).
Collection for professional certifications. Documents are publicly readable and only writable by the administrator.
Collection for images displayed in the portfolio gallery. Documents are publicly readable and only writable by the administrator.
Collection for contact messages submitted via the public form. Documents are publicly writable (unauthenticated create) but only readable and deletable by the administrator.

Singleton document storing global site configurations and content. Publicly readable via 'get' operation, but only writable by the administrator. Document ID is fixed to 'settings' for predictable access.
Collection for grouping related skills. Documents are publicly readable and only writable by the administrator.

Subcollection for specific technical skills, nested under their respective categories. Documents are publicly readable and only writable by the administrator. The 'skillCategoryId' is inherently part of the path for clear relationship modeling.

firestore.reasoning: The Firestore structure is designed following the core principles of Authorization Independence, Structural Segregation, and clear Access Modeling to ensure robust security, scalability, and debuggability for Rohan Bodkhe's portfolio and its Admin CMS. Authorization Independence is primarily achieved through a dedicated `/admins/{adminId}` collection. This collection acts as the single source of truth for administrator roles, where `{adminId}` directly corresponds to `request.auth.uid`. All admin-level operations (creating, updating, deleting content, reading contact messages, updating site settings) will reference this collection via a simple `exists(/databases/$(database)/documents/admins/$(request.auth.uid))` check in security rules, thereby eliminating complex `get()` calls that create hierarchical authorization dependencies and break atomic operations. This design choice makes rules explicit, atomic, and easy to debug. Structural Segregation ensures that all documents within a given collection share a homogeneous security posture. Publicly viewable content (Projects, Posts, Certifications, Gallery Items, Education, Skill Categories, Skills, and Site Settings) resides in top-level collections or logically nested subcollections to facilitate simple public read access. Collections like `/contactMessages` are configured for public write but admin-only read access. This prevents mixing data with different access requirements and simplifies security rules. For QAPs (Queries Are Not Filters), the structure supports secure `list` operations by leveraging Firebase Security Rules to enforce necessary conditions (e.g., `resource.data.status == 'published'`) for public reads on collections like `/posts` and `/projects`. This prevents unauthorized `list` queries from returning draft or private content. Admin users, identified by their presence in `/admins`, will have broader read/write access where appropriate, without needing complex client-side filtering that could expose sensitive data. The `SiteSettings` entity is modeled as a singleton document at `/siteSettings/settings`, allowing simple public `get` access while restricting `update` operations to the authenticated administrator. The relationship between `SkillCategory` and `Skill` is modeled using a hierarchical path `/skillCategories/{skillCategoryId}/skills/{skillId}`, aligning with the 'Continue Hierarchy for Nested Data' mandate, making the relationship clear and enabling efficient queries for skills within a specific category or collection group queries for all skills.
